o: — Eso pido, y barras derechas —dijo Sancho—; a eso me atengo, porque todo, al pie de la letra, ha de suceder por vuestra merced, llamándose el Caballero de la Triste Figura.
t: "That is what I ask for, and straight-laced," said Sancho; "that is what I stick to, because everything, to the letter, must come about through your grace, since you are called the Knight of the Sorrowful Countenance."

o: — No lo dudes, Sancho —replicó don Quijote—, porque del mesmo y por los mesmos pasos que esto he contado suben y han subido los caballeros andantes a ser reyes y emperadores.
t: "Do not doubt it, Sancho," replied Don Quixote, "because by the very same path and by the very same steps that I have been recounting, the knights-errant have risen and risen to be kings and emperors."

o: Sólo falta agora mirar qué rey de los cristianos o de los paganos tenga guerra y tenga hija hermosa; pero tiempo habrá para pensar esto, pues, como te tengo dicho, primero se ha de cobrar fama por otras partes que se acuda a la corte.
t: All that remains now is to see which king, Christian or pagan, is at war and has a beautiful daughter; but there will be time enough to think this over, since, as I have told you, fame must first be won elsewhere before one goes to court.

o: Así que, por esta falta, temo perder lo que mi brazo tiene bien merecido.
t: So, for want of that, I fear to lose what my arm has so well deserved.

o: Bien es verdad que yo soy hijodalgo de solar conocido, de posesión y propriedad y de devengar quinientos sueldos; y podría ser que el sabio que escribiese mi historia deslindase de tal manera mi parentela y decendencia, que me hallase quinto o sesto nieto de rey.
t: It is true enough that I am a hidalgo of known lineage, of estate and property, and entitled to five hundred ducats; and it could be that the wise man who wrote my history should set out my kinship and descent in such a way that he found me to be the fifth or sixth grandson of a king.

o: Porque te hago saber, Sancho, que hay dos maneras de linajes en el mundo: unos que traen y derriban su decendencia de príncipes y monarcas, a quien poco a poco el tiempo ha deshecho, y han acabado en punta, como pirámide puesta al revés; otros tuvieron principio de gente baja, y van subiendo de grado en grado, hasta llegar a ser grandes señores.
t: Because I tell you, Sancho, there are two kinds of lineage in the world: some that trace and bring down their descent from princes and monarchs, whom little by little time has undone, and who have ended in a point, like a pyramid set upside down; others had their beginning in humble folk, and go rising grade by grade until they become great lords.

o: De manera que está la diferencia en que unos fueron, que ya no son, y otros son, que ya no fueron; y podría ser yo déstos que, después de averiguado, hubiese sido mi principio grande y famoso, con lo cual se debía de contentar el rey, mi suegro, que hubiere de ser.
t: So that the difference lies in this: some were, and now are not, and others are, and now were not; and it might be that I am one of those whose beginning, once ascertained, was great and famous, with which the king, my father-in-law, who is to be, ought to be content.

o: Y cuando no, la infanta me ha de querer de manera que, a pesar de su padre, aunque claramente sepa que soy hijo de un azacán, me ha de admitir por señor y por esposo; y si no, aquí entra el roballa y llevalla donde más gusto me diere; que el tiempo o la muerte ha de acabar el enojo de sus padres.
t: And if not, the infanta must love me in such a way that, in spite of her father, even if she plainly knows I am the son of an Azacan, she must accept me as her lord and husband; and if not, here we come to carrying her off and taking her wherever I please; for time or death must put an end to her parents' anger.

o: — Ahí entra bien también —dijo Sancho— lo que algunos desalmados dicen: "No pidas de grado lo que puedes tomar por fuerza"; aunque mejor cuadra decir: "Más vale salto de mata que ruego de hombres buenos".
t: "That comes in well too," said Sancho, "what some God-forsaken people say: 'Do not ask by favor what you can take by force'; though it fits better to say: 'A leap over the hedge is better than a plea to good men.'"

o: Dígolo porque si el señor rey, suegro de vuestra merced, no se quisiere domeñar a entregalle a mi señora la infanta, no hay sino, como vuestra merced dice, roballa y trasponella.
t: I say so because if the king, your Grace's father-in-law, will not be brought to reason and give up my lady the Infanta to you, then there is nothing for it but, as your Grace says, to carry her off by force and run away with her.

o: Pero está el daño que, en tanto que se hagan las paces y se goce pacíficamente el reino, el pobre escudero se podrá estar a diente en esto de las mercedes.
t: But here is the harm: while peace is being made and the kingdom enjoyed in peace, the poor squire may yet get a bite of this business of the grants.

o: Si ya no es que la doncella tercera, que ha de ser su mujer, se sale con la infanta, y él pasa con ella su mala ventura, hasta que el cielo ordene otra cosa; porque bien podrá, creo yo, desde luego dársela su señor por ligítima esposa.
t: Unless it be that the third damsel, who is to be his wife, gets away with the Infanta, and he goes off with her and his ill luck, until Heaven orders otherwise; for I think his lord may well give her to him at once as his lawful wife.

o: — Eso no hay quien la quite —dijo don Quijote.
t: — That cannot be denied —said Don Quixote.

o: — Pues, como eso sea —respondió Sancho—, no hay sino encomendarnos a Dios, y dejar correr la suerte por donde mejor lo encaminare.
t: — Well, then, if that is so —answered Sancho— all we can do is commend ourselves to God and let fortune run where she may best direct it.

o: — Hágalo Dios —respondió don Quijote— como yo deseo y tú, Sancho, has menester; y ruin sea quien por ruin se tiene.
t: — May God do so —answered Don Quixote— as I wish and as you, Sancho, have need of; and cursed be whoever holds himself base.

o: — Sea par Dios —dijo Sancho—, que yo cristiano viejo soy, y para ser conde esto me basta.
t: — God willing —said Sancho— I am an old Christian, and that is enough for me to be a count.

o: — Y aun te sobra —dijo don Quijote—; y cuando no lo fueras, no hacía nada al caso, porque, siendo yo el rey, bien te puedo dar nobleza, sin que la compres ni me sirvas con nada.
t: — And you would have more than enough —said Don Quixote—; and even if you were not, it would make no difference, for, since I am the king, I can grant you nobility without your buying it or serving me in any way.

o: Porque, en haciéndote conde, cátate ahí caballero, y digan lo que dijeren; que a buena fe que te han de llamar señoría, mal que les pese.
t: Because once I make you a count, look you, there you are a knight, and let them say what they will; on my word, they shall call you 'Your Lordship', whether they like it or not.

o: — Y ¡montas que no sabría yo autorizar el litado!
t: — And how do you suppose I would know how to authorize the titled man!

o: — Dictado has de decir, que no litado —dijo su amo.
t: — You must say 'dictado', not 'litado' —said his master.

o: — Sea ansí —respondió Sancho Panza—.
t: — So be it —answered Sancho Panza—.

o: Digo que le sabría bien acomodar, porque, por vida mía, que un tiempo fui muñidor de una cofradía, y que me asentaba tan bien la ropa de muñidor, que decían todos que tenía presencia para poder ser prioste de la mesma cofradía.
t: I tell you he would suit me well, because, by my life, I was once the standard-bearer of a confraternity, and the standard-bearer's robe sat on me so well that everyone said I had the bearing to be the steward of that same confraternity.

o: Pues, ¿qué será cuando me ponga un ropón ducal a cuestas, o me vista de oro y de perlas, a uso de conde estranjero?
t: Well, then, what will it be when I have a ducal cloak on my back, or am dressed in gold and pearls, after the fashion of a foreign count?

o: Para mí tengo que me han de venir a ver de cien leguas.
t: For my part, I am sure they will come to see me from a hundred leagues away.

o: — Bien parecerás —dijo don Quijote—, pero será menester que te rapes las barbas a menudo; que, según las tienes de espesas, aborrascadas y mal puestas, si no te las rapas a navaja, cada dos días por lo menos, a tiro de escopeta se echará de ver lo que eres.
t: — You will look fine —said Don Quixote— but you will have to shave your beard often; for, thick, tangled and ill-trimmed as it is, if you do not shave it with a razor at least every other day, they will make out what you are at musket-shot range.

o: — ¿Qué hay más —dijo Sancho—, sino tomar un barbero y tenelle asalariado en casa?
t: — What is there more to do —said Sancho— than to hire a barber and keep him on salary at home?

o: Y aun, si fuere menester, le haré que ande tras mí, como caballerizo de grande.
t: And if need be, I shall have him running about after me, like a great lord's groom.

o: — Pues, ¿cómo sabes tú —preguntó don Quijote— que los grandes llevan detrás de sí a sus caballerizos?
t: — How do you know —asked Don Quixote— that great lords have their grooms behind them?

o: — Yo se lo diré —respondió Sancho—: los años pasados estuve un mes en la corte, y allí vi que, paseándose un señor muy pequeño, que decían que era muy grande, un hombre le seguía a caballo a todas las vueltas que daba, que no parecía sino que era su rabo.
t: — I will tell you —answered Sancho—: some years ago I spent a month at court, and there I saw that, as a very small gentleman, whom they said was a very great one, was taking a stroll, a man followed him on horseback wherever he turned, and it looked as though he were nothing but his tail.

o: Pregunté que cómo aquel hombre no se juntaba con el otro, sino que siempre andaba tras dél.
t: I asked how it was that that man did not join up with the other, but was always following him about.

o: Respondiéronme que era su caballerizo y que era uso de los grandes llevar tras sí a los tales.
t: They told me he was his groom, and that it was the custom of the great lords to keep such men in their train.

o: Desde entonces lo sé tan bien que nunca se me ha olvidado.
t: Since then I have known it so well that it has never slipped my memory.

o: — Digo que tienes razón —dijo don Quijote—, y que así puedes tú llevar a tu barbero; que los usos no vinieron todos juntos, ni se inventaron a una, y puedes ser tú el primero conde que lleve tras sí su barbero; y aun es de más confianza el hacer la barba que ensillar un caballo.
t: "I say you are right," said Don Quixote, "and that so you may take your barber along with you; for customs did not all come at once, nor were they all invented in a single day, and you may be the first count to have his barber trailing behind him; and shaving is a more trustworthy trade than saddling a horse."

o: — Quédese eso del barbero a mi cargo —dijo Sancho—, y al de vuestra merced se quede el procurar venir a ser rey y el hacerme conde.
t: "Leave the barber to my charge," said Sancho, "and let your Grace's business be to try to become king and make me a count."

o: — Así será —respondió don Quijote.
t: "So it shall be," replied Don Quixote.

o: Y, alzando los ojos, vio lo que se dirá en el siguiente capítulo.
t: And, raising his eyes, he saw what is told in the following chapter.

o: De la libertad que dio don Quijote a muchos desdichados que, mal de su grado, los llevaban donde no quisieran ir.
t: Of the freedom Don Quixote gave to many wretched men whom, against their will, they were carrying off to places they had no wish to go.

o: Venían ansimismo con ellos dos hombres de a caballo y dos de a pie; los de a caballo, con escopetas de rueda, y los de a pie, con dardos y espadas; y que así como Sancho Panza los vido, dijo.
t: There came likewise along with them two men on horseback and two on foot; the horsemen with wheel-lock muskets, and the footmen with javelins and swords; and, as Sancho Panza saw them, he said.

o: — Ésta es cadena de galeotes, gente forzada del rey, que va a las galeras.
t: "This is a chain of galley slaves, forced men of the king, who are going to the galleys."

o: — ¿Cómo gente forzada?
t: "Forced men?"

o: —preguntó don Quijote—.
t: "asked Don Quixote.

o: ¿Es posible que el rey haga fuerza a ninguna gente?
t: "Is it possible that the king should use force against any of his people?"

o: — No digo eso —respondió Sancho—, sino que es gente que, por sus delitos, va condenada a servir al rey en las galeras de por fuerza.
t: "I am not saying that," answered Sancho, "but I mean that these are men who, for their offenses, are condemned to serve the king in the galleys by force."

o: — En resolución —replicó don Quijote—, comoquiera que ello sea, esta gente, aunque los llevan, van de por fuerza, y no de su voluntad.
t: "In short," replied Don Quixote, "however it may be, these men, though they are being led along, are going by force and not of their own will."

o: — Así es —dijo Sancho.
t: "That is so," said Sancho.

o: — Pues desa manera —dijo su amo—, aquí encaja la ejecución de mi oficio: desfacer fuerzas y socorrer y acudir a los miserables.
t: "Then in that case," said his master, "here is where the exercise of my office comes in: to undo wrongs and to succor and aid the wretched."

o: — Advierta vuestra merced —dijo Sancho— que la justicia, que es el mesmo rey, no hace fuerza ni agravio a semejante gente, sino que los castiga en pena de sus delitos.
t: "Let your Grace take notice," said Sancho, "that justice, which is the king himself, does no violence nor injury to such men, but punishes them in penalty for their offenses."

o: Llegó, en esto, la cadena de los galeotes, y don Quijote, con muy corteses razones, pidió a los que iban en su guarda fuesen servidos de informalle y decille la causa, o causas, por que llevan aquella gente de aquella manera.
t: At that moment the chain of galley slaves arrived, and Don Quixote, with very courteous words, asked those who had them in custody to be so good as to inform him and tell him the cause, or causes, for which they were leading that people in that manner.

o: Una de las guardas de a caballo respondió que eran galeotes, gente de Su Majestad que iba a galeras, y que no había más que decir, ni él tenía más que saber.
t: One of the mounted guards replied that they were galley slaves, subjects of His Majesty who were being sent to the galleys, and that there was nothing more to say, nor was there anything else he needed to know.

o: — Con todo eso —replicó don Quijote—, querría saber de cada uno dellos en particular la causa de su desgracia.
t: "All the same," replied Don Quixote, "I should like to know from each of them in particular the cause of his misfortune."

o: Con esta licencia, que don Quijote se tomara aunque no se la dieran, se llegó a la cadena, y al primero le preguntó que por qué pecados iba de tan mala guisa.
t: With this license, which Don Quixote took upon himself though it was not granted him, he approached the chain, and asked the first of them why he was going about in such a sorry state.

o: Él le respondió que por enamorado iba de aquella manera.
t: He replied that he was going that way for love.

o: —replicó don Quijote—.
t: "replied Don Quixote."

o: Pues, si por enamorados echan a galeras, días ha que pudiera yo estar bogando en ellas.
t: "Well, if it is for love that they send men to the galleys, I could have been rowing in them for some days now."

o: — No son los amores como los que vuestra merced piensa —dijo el galeote—; que los míos fueron que quise tanto a una canasta de colar, atestada de ropa blanca, que la abracé conmigo tan fuertemente que, a no quitármela la justicia por fuerza, aún hasta agora no la hubiera dejado de mi voluntad.
t: "The loves are not like the ones your Grace supposes," said the galley slave; "mine were like this: I wanted a wicker basket of white linen so dearly that I hugged it to me so tightly that, had the law not taken it from me by force, even now I would not have let it go of my own will."

o: Fue en fragante, no hubo lugar de tormento; concluyóse la causa, acomodáronme las espaldas con ciento, y por añadidura tres precisos de gurapas, y acabóse la obra.
t: He was taken in the act; there was no need for any torture; his case was closed, they flogged his back with a hundred lashes, and by way of addition three good kicks, and there the business was done.

o: — ¿Qué son gurapas?
t: "What are kicks?"

o: —preguntó don Quijote.
t: "— asked Don Quixote.

o: — Gurapas son galeras —respondió el galeote.
t: "Kicks are galleys," answered the galley slave.

o: El cual era un mozo de hasta edad de veinte y cuatro años, y dijo que era natural de Piedrahíta.
t: He was a young man of about twenty-four years of age, and said he was a native of Piedrahíta.

o: Lo mesmo preguntó don Quijote al segundo, el cual no respondió palabra, según iba de triste y malencónico; mas respondió por él el primero, y dijo.
t: Don Quixote asked the second the same question, but he said not a word, so sad and melancholy was he; the first answered for him, saying:

o: — Éste, señor, va por canario; digo, por músico y cantor.
t: "This one, sir, is going for a canary; that is, for a musician and singer."

o: — Pues, ¿cómo —repitió don Quijote—, por músicos y cantores van también a galeras?
t: "Then how is it," repeated Don Quixote, "that musicians and singers also go to the galleys?"

o: — Sí, señor —respondió el galeote—, que no hay peor cosa que cantar en el ansia.
t: "Yes, sir," answered the galley slave, "for there is nothing worse than singing in one's distress."

o: — Antes, he yo oído decir —dijo don Quijote— que quien canta sus males espanta.
t: "I have heard it said before," said Don Quixote, "that whoever sings his sorrows drives them away."

o: — Acá es al revés —dijo el galeote—, que quien canta una vez llora toda la vida.
t: "Here it is the other way round," said the galley slave, "for whoever sings once weeps for life."

o: — No lo entiendo —dijo don Quijote.
t: "I don't understand," said Don Quixote.

o: Mas una de las guardas le dijo.
t: But one of the guards told him.

o: — Señor caballero, cantar en el ansia se dice, entre esta gente non santa, confesar en el tormento.
t: "Sir knight, singing in distress is what among this unsanctified folk means confessing under torture."

o: A este pecador le dieron tormento y confesó su delito, que era ser cuatrero, que es ser ladrón de bestias, y, por haber confesado, le condenaron por seis años a galeras, amén de docientos azotes que ya lleva en las espaldas.
t: This sinner was put to the torture and confessed his crime, which was being a cuatrero, that is, a thief of beasts, and, for having confessed, they sentenced him to six years in the galleys, amen to two hundred lashes he already carries on his back.

o: Y va siempre pensativo y triste, porque los demás ladrones que allá quedan y aquí van le maltratan y aniquilan, y escarnecen y tienen en poco, porque confesó y no tuvo ánimo de decir nones.
t: And he always goes pensive and sad, because the other thieves who stay there and come here mistreat and destroy him, and mock him and hold him in contempt, because he confessed and lacked the spirit to say no.

o: Porque dicen ellos que tantas letras tiene un no como un sí, y que harta ventura tiene un delincuente, que está en su lengua su vida o su muerte, y no en la de los testigos y probanzas; y para mí tengo que no van muy fuera de camino.
t: Because they say that a no has as many letters as a yes, and that a criminal is lucky indeed, for his life or death lies on his own tongue, and not on that of witnesses and evidence; and for my part, I have to say they are not far off the track.

o: — Y yo lo entiendo así —respondió don Quijote.
t: "And that is how I understand it too," replied Don Quixote.

o: El cual, pasando al tercero, preguntó lo que a los otros; el cual, de presto y con mucho desenfado, respondió y dijo.
t: He, passing on to the third, asked him the same as the others; who, promptly and with great assurance, answered and said:

o: — Yo voy por cinco años a las señoras gurapas por faltarme diez ducados.
t: "I am going for five years to the galleys for lacking ten ducats."

o: — Yo daré veinte de muy buena gana —dijo don Quijote— por libraros desa pesadumbre.
t: "I will give twenty, very willingly," said Don Quixote, "to rid you of that burden."

o: — Eso me parece —respondió el galeote— como quien tiene dineros en mitad del golfo y se está muriendo de hambre, sin tener adonde comprar lo que ha menester.
t: "That strikes me," replied the galley slave, "like someone who has money in the middle of the gulf and is starving, with nowhere to buy what he needs."

o: Dígolo porque si a su tiempo tuviera yo esos veinte ducados que vuestra merced ahora me ofrece, hubiera untado con ellos la péndola del escribano y avivado el ingenio del procurador, de manera que hoy me viera en mitad de la plaza de Zocodover, de Toledo, y no en este camino, atraillado como galgo; pero Dios es grande: paciencia y basta.
t: I say this because, if in due time I had those twenty ducats your grace is now offering me, I would have used them to grease the clerk's pen and sharpen the lawyer's wit, so that today you would see me in the middle of the square of Zocodover in Toledo, and not on this road, harnessed like a greyhound; but God is great: patience, and that is enough.

o: Pasó don Quijote al cuarto, que era un hombre de venerable rostro con una barba blanca que le pasaba del pecho; el cual, oyéndose preguntar la causa por que allí venía, comenzó a llorar y no respondió palabra; mas el quinto condenado le sirvió de lengua, y dijo.
t: Don Quixote passed on to the fourth, who was a man of venerable countenance with a white beard that reached past his chest; who, on hearing himself asked the reason for which he was there, began to weep and said nothing in reply; but the fifth condemned man served him as tongue, and said:

o: — Este hombre honrado va por cuatro años a galeras, habiendo paseado las acostumbradas vestido en pompa y a caballo.
t: "This worthy man is going to the galleys for four years, after having strutted about in the usual pomp and on horseback."

o: — Eso es —dijo Sancho Panza—, a lo que a mí me parece, haber salido a la vergüenza.
t: "That is so," said Sancho Panza, "in my view, having gone out to public disgrace."

o: — Así es —replicó el galeote—; y la culpa por que le dieron esta pena es por haber sido corredor de oreja, y aun de todo el cuerpo.
t: "So it is," replied the galley slave; "and the fault for which they gave him this sentence is for having been a pimp, and indeed of the whole body."

o: En efecto, quiero decir que este caballero va por alcahuete, y por tener asimesmo sus puntas y collar de hechicero.
t: In truth, I mean to say that this gentleman is going as a pimp, and for having, as it were, the tips and collar of a wizard.

o: Quisiera pasar adelante y dar las razones por que convenía hacer elección de los que en la república habían de tener tan necesario oficio, pero no es el lugar acomodado para ello: algún día lo diré a quien lo pueda proveer y remediar.
t: I would like to go further and give the reasons why it befits the republic to choose those who are to hold so necessary an office; but this is not the suitable place for it: some day I will say it to whoever can provide and remedy it.

o: Sólo digo ahora que la pena que me ha causado ver estas blancas canas y este rostro venerable en tanta fatiga, por alcahuete, me la ha quitado el adjunto de ser hechicero; aunque bien sé que no hay hechizos en el mundo que puedan mover y forzar la voluntad, como algunos simples piensan; que es libre nuestro albedrío, y no hay yerba ni encanto que le fuerce.
t: I will say only now that the pain it caused me to see these white hairs and this venerable face in such hardship, for being a pimp, has taken from me the charge of being a wizard; though well do I know that there are no spells in the world that can move and force the will, as some simple folk suppose; for our free choice is free, and there is no herb or enchantment that can constrain it.

o: Lo que suelen hacer algunas mujercillas simples y algunos embusteros bellacos es algunas misturas y venenos con que vuelven locos a los hombres, dando a entender que tienen fuerza para hacer querer bien, siendo, como digo, cosa imposible forzar la voluntad.
t: What some simple little women and some crafty rogues usually do is make certain mixtures and poisons with which they drive men mad, giving to understand that they have the power to make men love them, which, as I say, is an impossible thing, to force the will.

o: — Así es —dijo el buen viejo—, y, en verdad, señor, que en lo de hechicero que no tuve culpa; en lo de alcahuete, no lo pude negar.
t: "So it is," said the good old man; "and, truly, sir, as to being a wizard I was not to blame; as to being a pimp, I could not deny it."

o: Pero nunca pensé que hacía mal en ello: que toda mi intención era que todo el mundo se holgase y viviese en paz y quietud, sin pendencias ni penas; pero no me aprovechó nada este buen deseo para dejar de ir adonde no espero volver, según me cargan los años y un mal de orina que llevo, que no me deja reposar un rato.
t: But I never thought I was doing wrong in it: for all my intention was that everyone might enjoy themselves and live in peace and quiet, without quarrels or troubles; but this good wish did me no good to keep me from going where I do not expect to return, as my years and a bad urinary condition, which I carry with me and which will not let me rest for a moment, weigh me down.

o: Y aquí tornó a su llanto, como de primero; y túvole Sancho tanta compasión, que sacó un real de a cuatro del seno y se le dio de limosna.
t: And here he burst into tears again, as at first; and Sancho was so moved with compassion that he took a four-real piece from his bosom and gave it to him as alms.

o: Pasó adelante don Quijote, y preguntó a otro su delito, el cual respondió con no menos, sino con mucha más gallardía que el pasado.
t: Don Quixote passed on and asked another his crime, who replied with no less, but with much more gallantry than the previous one.

o: — Yo voy aquí porque me burlé demasiadamente con dos primas hermanas mías, y con otras dos hermanas que no lo eran mías; finalmente, tanto me burlé con todas, que resultó de la burla crecer la parentela, tan intricadamente que no hay diablo que la declare.
t: — I am here because I mocked two of my cousins too much, and two other sisters who were not mine of kin; in the end, so much did I mock them all that the joking gave rise to such a tangled web of relatives that there is no devil who could set it straight.

o: Probóseme todo, faltó favor, no tuve dineros, víame a pique de perder los tragaderos, sentenciáronme a galeras por seis años, consentí: castigo es de mi culpa; mozo soy: dure la vida, que con ella todo se alcanza.
t: They tried me for everything; favour failed me, I had no money, I saw myself on the point of losing my very throat, and they sentenced me to the galleys for six years. I consented: the punishment is of my own making; I am still a young man: let life endure, for with it everything is attained.

o: Si vuestra merced, señor caballero, lleva alguna cosa con que socorrer a estos pobretes, Dios se lo pagará en el cielo, y nosotros tendremos en la tierra cuidado de rogar a Dios en nuestras oraciones por la vida y salud de vuestra merced, que sea tan larga y tan buena como su buena presencia merece.
t: If your worship, sir knight, carries anything with which to succour these poor wretches, may God repay you in heaven, and we on earth will take care to pray to God in our prayers for your life and health, may it be as long and as good as your good presence deserves.

o: Éste iba en hábito de estudiante, y dijo una de las guardas que era muy grande hablador y muy gentil latino.
t: This one was dressed as a student, and one of the guards said he was a great talker and a very elegant Latin scholar.

o: Tras todos éstos, venía un hombre de muy buen parecer, de edad de treinta años, sino que al mirar metía el un ojo en el otro un poco.
t: After all these came a man of very good appearance, about thirty years old, except that when he looked he put one eye into the other a little.

o: Preguntó don Quijote que cómo iba aquel hombre con tantas prisiones más que los otros.
t: Don Quixote asked how that man was going with so many more irons than the others.

o: Respondióle la guarda porque tenía aquel solo más delitos que todos los otros juntos, y que era tan atrevido y tan grande bellaco que, aunque le llevaban de aquella manera, no iban seguros dél, sino que temían que se les había de huir.
t: The guard replied that he had alone more crimes than all the others put together, and that he was so bold and such a great rogue that even though they were taking him along in that manner, they did not feel safe with him, for they feared he would slip away from them.

o: — ¿Qué delitos puede tener —dijo don Quijote—, si no han merecido más pena que echalle a las galeras?
t: — What crimes can he have —said Don Quixote— if they have deserved no greater punishment than being sent to the galleys?

o: — Va por diez años —replicó la guarda—, que es como muerte cevil.
t: — He is going for ten years —replied the guard— which is like a civil death.

o: No se quiera saber más, sino que este buen hombre es el famoso Ginés de Pasamonte, que por otro nombre llaman Ginesillo de Parapilla.
t: Let no one try to know more, for this good man is the famous Ginés de Pasamonte, who by another name is called Ginesillo de Parapilla.

o: — Señor comisario —dijo entonces el galeote—, váyase poco a poco, y no andemos ahora a deslindar nombres y sobrenombres.
t: — Sir commissary —said the galley slave then— go gently, and let us not now go about sifting names and nicknames.

o: Ginés me llamo y no Ginesillo, y Pasamonte es mi alcurnia, y no Parapilla, como voacé dice; y cada uno se dé una vuelta a la redonda, y no hará poco.
t: My name is Ginés and not Ginesillo, and Pasamonte is my birthplace, and not Parapilla, as your honour says; and let each man give himself a turn of the circle, and he will do no harm.

o: — Hable con menos tono —replicó el comisario—, señor ladrón de más de la marca, si no quiere que le haga callar, mal que le pese.
t: — Speak with less airs —replied the commissary— you thief of the worst sort, unless you want me to make you silent, whether you like it or not.

o: — Bien parece —respondió el galeote— que va el hombre como Dios es servido, pero algún día sabrá alguno si me llamo Ginesillo de Parapilla o no.
t: — It seems fitting —answered the galley slave— that the man goes as God is served, but some day someone will know whether I am called Ginesillo de Parapilla or not.

o: — Pues, ¿no te llaman ansí, embustero? —dijo la guarda.
t: — Well, is that not what they call you, you cheat? —said the guard.

o: — Sí llaman —respondió Ginés—, mas yo haré que no me lo llamen, o me las pelaría donde yo digo entre mis dientes.
t: — That is what they call me —answered Ginés— but I shall make them not call me so, or I shall settle it with them where I say, between my teeth.

o: Señor caballero, si tiene algo que darnos, dénoslo ya, y vaya con Dios, que ya enfada con tanto querer saber vidas ajenas; y si la mía quiere saber, sepa que yo soy Ginés de Pasamonte, cuya vida está escrita por estos pulgares.
t: Sir knight, if you have anything to give us, give it us now, and go with God, for you already grow tiresome with so much prying into other men's lives; and if you would know mine, know that I am Ginés de Pasamonte, whose life is written by these very thumbs.

o: — Dice verdad —dijo el comisario—: que él mesmo ha escrito su historia, que no hay más, y deja empeñado el libro en la cárcel en docientos reales.
t: — He tells the truth —said the commissary—: he has written his own history himself, and that is all, and he leaves the book pledged in the jail for two hundred reals.

o: — Y le pienso quitar —dijo Ginés—, si quedara en docientos ducados.
t: — And I mean to take it from him —said Ginés— if it were left for two hundred ducats.

o: —dijo don Quijote.
t: "said Don Quixote.

o: — Es tan bueno —respondió Ginés— que mal año para Lazarillo de Tormes y para todos cuantos de aquel género se han escrito o escribieren.
t: — He is so good —answered Ginés— that a bad year for Lazarillo de Tormes and for all others of that sort who have been written or shall be written.

o: Lo que le sé decir a voacé es que trata verdades, y que son verdades tan lindas y tan donosas que no pueden haber mentiras que se le igualen.
t: All I can tell your worship is that he tells the truth, and such fine and dainty truths that no lies could match them.

o: — ¿Y cómo se intitula el libro?
t: "And what is the book called?"

o: —preguntó don Quijote.
t: "— asked Don Quixote.

o: — La vida de Ginés de Pasamonte —respondió el mismo.
t: "The Life of Ginés de Pasamonte," he replied.

o: — ¿Y está acabado?
t: "And is it finished?"

o: —preguntó don Quijote.
t: "— asked Don Quixote.

o: — ¿Cómo puede estar acabado —respondió él—, si aún no está acabada mi vida?
t: "How could it be finished," he answered, "when my life is not yet finished?"

o: Lo que está escrito es desde mi nacimiento hasta el punto que esta última vez me han echado en galeras.
t: What is written runs from my birth up to the point where they put me in the galleys for the last time.

o: — Luego, ¿otra vez habéis estado en ellas?
t: "So you have been in the galleys again?"

o: —dijo don Quijote.
t: "said Don Quixote.

o: — Hábil pareces —dijo don Quijote.
t: "You seem clever," said Don Quixote.

o: — Y desdichado —respondió Ginés—; porque siempre las desdichas persiguen al buen ingenio.
t: "And unlucky," replied Ginés, "for misfortunes always pursue good talent."

o: — Persiguen a los bellacos —dijo el comisario.
t: "They pursue rogues," said the commissary.

o: — Ya le he dicho, señor comisario —respondió Pasamonte—, que se vaya poco a poco, que aquellos señores no le dieron esa vara para que maltratase a los pobretes que aquí vamos, sino para que nos guiase y llevase adonde Su Majestad manda.
t: "I have already told you, sir commissary," replied Pasamonte, "that you may go about your business, for those gentlemen did not give you that staff to mistreat the poor wretches like us who are here, but to guide us and take us where His Majesty commands."

o: Si no, ¡por vida de...!
t: If not, by my life...!

o: ¡Basta!, que podría ser que saliesen algún día en la colada las manchas que se hicieron en la venta; y todo el mundo calle, y viva bien, y hable mejor y caminemos, que ya es mucho regodeo éste.
t: Enough! It could be that someday the stains made at the inn should come out in the wash; and let everyone keep quiet, live well, speak better, and let us get going, for there has been enough fuss already.

o: Alzó la vara en alto el comisario para dar a Pasamonte en respuesta de sus amenazas, mas don Quijote se puso en medio y le rogó que no le maltratase, pues no era mucho que quien llevaba tan atadas las manos tuviese algún tanto suelta la lengua.
t: The commissary raised his staff high, to answer Pasamonte's threats with one of his own, but Don Quixote stepped in between and begged him not to mistreat the man, since it was hardly much that one whose hands were so tightly bound should have his tongue somewhat loose.

o: Todo lo cual se me representa a mí ahora en la memoria de manera que me está diciendo, persuadiendo y aun forzando que muestre con vosotros el efeto para que el cielo me arrojó al mundo, y me hizo profesar en él la orden de caballería que profeso, y el voto que en ella hice de favorecer a los menesterosos y opresos de los mayores.
t: All of which is now brought to my memory in such a way that it seems to be telling me, persuading me, even forcing me, to show you the effect of it, so that heaven, which cast me into the world, made me profess in it the order of chivalry that I profess, and the vow I made in it to favor the needy and the oppressed among the powerful.

o: Pero, porque sé que una de las partes de la prudencia es que lo que se puede hacer por bien no se haga por mal, quiero rogar a estos señores guardianes y comisario sean servidos de desataros y dejaros ir en paz, que no faltarán otros que sirvan al rey en mejores ocasiones; porque me parece duro caso hacer esclavos a los que Dios y naturaleza hizo libres.
t: But because I know that one part of prudence is that what can be done for good should not be done for harm, I wish to ask these gentlemen, your guards and commissary, to be so kind as to untie us and let us go in peace; there will not lack others to serve the king on better occasions; for it seems to me a harsh thing to make slaves of those whom God and nature made free.

o: Cuanto más, señores guardas —añadió don Quijote—, que estos pobres no han cometido nada contra vosotros.
t: Moreover, gentlemen guards," added Don Quixote, "these poor men have committed no offense against you."

o: Allá se lo haya cada uno con su pecado; Dios hay en el cielo, que no se descuida de castigar al malo ni de premiar al bueno, y no es bien que los hombres honrados sean verdugos de los otros hombres, no yéndoles nada en ello.
t: Let every one answer for his own sin; God is in heaven, and he does not neglect to punish the wicked or to reward the good, and it is not fitting that honest men should be the executioners of other men, gaining nothing by it.

o: Pido esto con esta mansedumbre y sosiego, porque tenga, si lo cumplís, algo que agradeceros; y, cuando de grado no lo hagáis, esta lanza y esta espada, con el valor de mi brazo, harán que lo hagáis por fuerza.
t: I ask this with all this gentleness and calm, so that if you grant it you may have something to thank me for; and if you do not do it of your own will, this lance and this sword, with the strength of my arm, will make you do it by force.

o: — ¡Donosa majadería!
t: "What a dainty piece of folly!"

o: —respondió el comisario— ¡Bueno está el donaire con que ha salido a cabo de rato!
t: "—answered the commissary— well, there's fine grace with which he made off a while ago!"

o: ¡Los forzados del rey quiere que le dejemos, como si tuviéramos autoridad para soltarlos o él la tuviera para mandárnoslo!
t: "The king's convicts he wants us to let go, as if we had the authority to release them, or he the authority to order us to do it!"

o: Váyase vuestra merced, señor, norabuena, su camino adelante, y enderécese ese bacín que trae en la cabeza, y no ande buscando tres pies al gato.
t: "Off with you, your worship, sir, good luck to you, straight along your road, and set that basin on your head straight, and stop looking for three legs on a cat."

o: — ¡Vos sois el gato, y el rato, y el bellaco!
t: "You are the cat, and the rat, and the rogue!"

o: —respondió don Quijote.
t: "replied Don Quixote.

o: Y, diciendo y haciendo, arremetió con él tan presto que, sin que tuviese lugar de ponerse en defensa, dio con él en el suelo, malherido de una lanzada; y avínole bien, que éste era el de la escopeta.
t: And, saying and doing this, he charged at him so swiftly that, before the other had time to put himself on the defensive, he brought him down to the ground, badly wounded with a thrust of the lance; and he did him good service, for this was the man with the shotgun.

o: Fue la revuelta de manera que las guardas, ya por acudir a los galeotes, que se desataban, ya por acometer a don Quijote, que los acometía, no hicieron cosa que fuese de provecho.
t: The uproar was such that the guards, whether from going to the galley slaves, who were breaking loose, or from attacking Don Quixote, who was attacking them, did nothing that was of any use.

o: Entristecióse mucho Sancho deste suceso, porque se le representó que los que iban huyendo habían de dar noticia del caso a la Santa Hermandad, la cual, a campana herida, saldría a buscar los delincuentes, y así se lo dijo a su amo, y le rogó que luego de allí se partiesen y se emboscasen en la sierra, que estaba cerca.
t: Sancho was much saddened by this affair, because it occurred to him that those who were fleeing would report the matter to the Holy Brotherhood, which, with bell rung full peal, would come out to hunt down the criminals; and so he told his master, and begged him to leave that place at once and hide in the mountains nearby.

o: — Bien está eso —dijo don Quijote—, pero yo sé lo que ahora conviene que se haga.
t: "That is well said," said Don Quixote, "but I know what must be done now."

o: Y, llamando a todos los galeotes, que andaban alborotados y habían despojado al comisario hasta dejarle en cueros, se le pusieron todos a la redonda para ver lo que les mandaba, y así les dijo.
t: And, calling all the galley slaves, who were in a uproar and had stripped the commissary until he was naked, they all gathered around him to see what he commanded them, and thus he spoke to them.

o: — De gente bien nacida es agradecer los beneficios que reciben, y uno de los pecados que más a Dios ofende es la ingratitud.
t: "It is the mark of good breeding to be grateful for the benefits one receives, and one of the sins that most offend God is ingratitude."

o: Respondió por todos Ginés de Pasamonte, y dijo.
t: Ginés de Pasamonte answered for all of them and said:

o: — Lo que vuestra merced nos manda, señor y libertador nuestro, es imposible de toda imposibilidad cumplirlo, porque no podemos ir juntos por los caminos, sino solos y divididos, y cada uno por su parte, procurando meterse en las entrañas de la tierra, por no ser hallado de la Santa Hermandad, que, sin duda alguna, ha de salir en nuestra busca.
t: "What your worship orders us, sir and our liberator, is impossible in every sense of the word, for we cannot go together along the roads, but alone and separated, each one on his own way, trying to hide ourselves in the bowels of the earth, so as not to be found by the Holy Brotherhood, which will undoubtedly come out to seek us."

o: — Pues ¡voto a tal!
t: "Well then, by my faith!"

o: —dijo don Quijote, ya puesto en cólera—, don hijo de la puta, don Ginesillo de Paropillo, o como os llamáis, que habéis de ir vos solo, rabo entre piernas, con toda la cadena a cuestas.
t: "—said Don Quixote, now in a fury— you son of a bitch, Don Ginesillo de Paropillo, or whatever your name is, you must go alone, tail between your legs, with the whole chain on your back."

o: Sancho se puso tras su asno, y con él se defendía de la nube y pedrisco que sobre entrambos llovía.
t: Sancho took shelter behind his donkey, and with it defended himself from the rain and hail that poured down on both of them.

o: No se pudo escudar tan bien don Quijote que no le acertasen no sé cuántos guijarros en el cuerpo, con tanta fuerza que dieron con él en el suelo; y apenas hubo caído, cuando fue sobre él el estudiante y le quitó la bacía de la cabeza, y diole con ella tres o cuatro golpes en las espaldas y otros tantos en la tierra, con que la hizo pedazos.
t: Don Quixote could not shield himself so well that they did not strike him, he knew not how many pebbles, on the body, with such force that they brought him down to the ground; and scarcely had he fallen when the student came down upon him and took the basin from his head, and dealt him three or four blows with it on the back and as many on the ground, and with them he smashed it to pieces.

o: Quitáronle una ropilla que traía sobre las armas, y las medias calzas le querían quitar si las grebas no lo estorbaran.
t: They took from him a jerkin he wore over his armor, and they would have taken off his hose too, had not the greaves hindered them.

o: A Sancho le quitaron el gabán, y, dejándole en pelota, repartiendo entre sí los demás despojos de la batalla, se fueron cada uno por su parte, con más cuidado de escaparse de la Hermandad, que temían, que de cargarse de la cadena e ir a presentarse ante la señora Dulcinea del Toboso.
t: They took Sancho's coat, and, leaving him in his shirt, sharing among themselves the rest of the spoils of the battle, they went each his own way, more concerned with escaping the Brotherhood, which they feared, than with burdening themselves with the chain and going to present themselves before the lady Dulcinea of Toboso.

o: De lo que le aconteció al famoso don Quijote en Sierra Morena, que fue una de las más raras aventuras que en esta verdadera historia se cuentan.
t: Of what happened to the famous Don Quixote in Sierra Morena, which was one of the strangest adventures recounted in this true history.

o: Viéndose tan malparado don Quijote, dijo a su escudero.
t: Seeing how battered he was, Don Quixote said to his squire.

o: — Siempre, Sancho, lo he oído decir, que el hacer bien a villanos es echar agua en la mar.
t: "Always, Sancho, I have heard it said that doing good to rogues is like throwing water into the sea."

o: Si yo hubiera creído lo que me dijiste, yo hubiera escusado esta pesadumbre; pero ya está hecho: paciencia, y escarmentar para desde aquí adelante.
t: Had I believed what you told me, I would have spared myself this trouble; but it is done: patience, and let us be on our guard from here on.

o: — Señor —respondió Sancho—, que el retirar no es huir, ni el esperar es cordura, cuando el peligro sobrepuja a la esperanza, y de sabios es guardarse hoy para mañana y no aventurarse todo en un día.
t: "Sir," replied Sancho, "retreating is not fleeing, nor is waiting wise, when danger outweighs hope; and it is the mark of the wise to guard themselves today for tomorrow and not to risk everything in a single day."

o: Y sepa que, aunque zafio y villano, todavía se me alcanza algo desto que llaman buen gobierno; así que, no se arrepienta de haber tomado mi consejo, sino suba en Rocinante, si puede, o si no yo le ayudaré, y sígame, que el caletre me dice que hemos menester ahora más los pies que las manos.
t: And know that, though clumsy and rustic, I still have some grasp of what they call good government; so do not regret having taken my advice, but mount Rocinante if you can, and if not I will help you, and follow me, for my pack tells me that right now we have more need of feet than of hands."

o: Subió don Quijote, sin replicarle más palabra, y, guiando Sancho sobre su asno, se entraron por una parte de Sierra Morena, que allí junto estaba, llevando Sancho intención de atravesarla toda e ir a salir al Viso, o a Almodóvar del Campo, y esconderse algunos días por aquellas asperezas, por no ser hallados si la Hermandad los buscase.
t: Don Quixote mounted without replying another word, and, with Sancho guiding him on his donkey, they entered by a stretch of Sierra Morena that lay close by, Sancho intending to cross it all and come out at El Viso, or at Almodóvar del Campo, and hide for a few days among those rough places, so as not to be found if the Brotherhood should be searching for them.

o: Animóle a esto haber visto que de la refriega de los galeotes se había escapado libre la despensa que sobre su asno venía, cosa que la juzgó a milagro, según fue lo que llevaron y buscaron los galeotes.
t: What urged him on to this was having seen that the pantry, which was strapped to his donkey, had come through the scuffle with the galley slaves unscathed, a thing he judged a miracle, considering what the galley slaves had carried off and searched for.

o: Así como don Quijote entró por aquellas montañas, se le alegró el corazón, pareciéndole aquellos lugares acomodados para las aventuras que buscaba.
t: As soon as Don Quixote entered among those mountains, his heart was glad, for those places seemed suited to the adventures he was seeking.

o: Reducíansele a la memoria los maravillosos acaecimientos que en semejantes soledades y asperezas habían sucedido a caballeros andantes.
t: The marvelous happenings that had befallen wandering knights in such lonely wilds and rough country came back to his memory.

o: Iba pensando en estas cosas, tan embebecido y trasportado en ellas que de ninguna otra se acordaba.
t: He went along thinking about these things, so absorbed and carried away by them that he remembered nothing else.

o: Hízolo con mucha presteza Sancho, y, aunque la maleta venía cerrada con una cadena y su candado, por lo roto y podrido della vio lo que en ella había, que eran cuatro camisas de delgada holanda y otras cosas de lienzo, no menos curiosas que limpias, y en un pañizuelo halló un buen montoncillo de escudos de oro; y, así como los vio, dijo.
t: Sancho did this very quickly, and, though the valise was closed with a chain and its padlock, through its battered and rotten state he saw what was inside, which were four shirts of fine holland and other linen things no less curious than clean, and in a kerchief he found a good little pile of gold coins; and, when he saw them, he said.

o: — ¡Bendito sea todo el cielo, que nos ha deparado una aventura que sea de provecho!
t: "Blessed be all heaven, which has brought us an adventure that will be of profit!"

o: Y buscando más, halló un librillo de memoria, ricamente guarnecido.
t: And searching further, he found a little memorandum book, richly bound.

o: Éste le pidió don Quijote, y mandóle que guardase el dinero y lo tomase para él.
t: Don Quixote asked for it and told him to keep the money and take it for him.

o: Besóle las manos Sancho por la merced, y, desvalijando a la valija de su lencería, la puso en el costal de la despensa.
t: Sancho kissed his hands in thanks, and, unpacking the valise of his bedding, put it into the pack of the pantry.

o: Todo lo cual visto por don Quijote, dijo.
t: All of which, seen by Don Quixote, he said.

o: — Paréceme, Sancho, y no es posible que sea otra cosa, que algún caminante descaminado debió de pasar por esta sierra, y, salteándole malandrines, le debieron de matar, y le trujeron a enterrar en esta tan escondida parte.
t: "It seems to me, Sancho, and it cannot be otherwise, that some wandering traveler must have passed through this sierra, and, being waylaid by rogues, they must have killed him and brought him here to be buried in this so hidden place."

o: — No puede ser eso —respondió Sancho—, porque si fueran ladrones, no se dejaran aquí este dinero.
t: "That cannot be," replied Sancho, "because if they were thieves, they would not have left this money here."

o: — Verdad dices —dijo don Quijote—, y así, no adivino ni doy en lo que esto pueda ser; mas, espérate: veremos si en este librillo de memoria hay alguna cosa escrita por donde podamos rastrear y venir en conocimiento de lo que deseamos.
t: "You are right," said Don Quixote, "and so I neither guess nor hit upon what this may be; but, wait: let us see if there is anything written in this memorandum book by which we may track things down and come to know what we wish."

o: Abrióle, y lo primero que halló en él escrito, como en borrador, aunque de muy buena letra, fue un soneto, que, leyéndole alto porque Sancho también lo oyese, vio que decía desta manera.
t: He opened it, and the first thing he found written in it, as in a draft, though in a very good hand, was a sonnet, which, reading it aloud so that Sancho might also hear it, he saw said thus.

o: O le falta al Amor conocimiento.
t: Or Love is lacking in knowledge.

o: o le sobra crueldad, o no es mi pena.
t: or it has too much cruelty, or it is not my pain

o: igual a la ocasión que me condena.
t: equal to the occasion that condemns me

o: al género más duro de tormento.
t: to the harshest kind of torment.

o: Pero si Amor es dios, es argumento.
t: But if Love is a god, it is an argument

o: que nada ignora, y es razón muy buena.
t: that ignores nothing, and it is very good reason

o: que un dios no sea cruel.
t: that a god should not be cruel.

o: Pues, ¿quién ordena.
t: Well, then, who orders

o: el terrible dolor que adoro y siento?
t: the terrible pain I adore and feel?

o: Si digo que sois vos, Fili, no acierto.
t: If I say that you are the one, Fili, I am not right.

o: que tanto mal en tanto bien no cabe.
t: that so much evil cannot be contained in so much good.

o: ni me viene del cielo esta rüina.
t: nor does this ruin come to me from heaven.

o: Presto habré de morir, que es lo más cierto.
t: Soon I must die, which is the most certain thing.

o: que al mal de quien la causa no se sabe.
t: for the ill of whoever's cause is not known:

o: milagro es acertar la medicina.
t: it is a miracle to find the right remedy.

o: — Por esa trova —dijo Sancho— no se puede saber nada, si ya no es que por ese hilo que está ahí se saque el ovillo de todo.
t: — For that riddle —said Sancho— nothing can be known, unless it is that by that thread which is there one draws out the whole skein.

o: — ¿Qué hilo está aquí?
t: — What thread is here?

o: —dijo don Quijote.
t: "said Don Quixote.

o: — Paréceme —dijo Sancho— que vuestra merced nombró ahí hilo.
t: — It seems to me —said Sancho— that your grace mentioned a thread there.

o: — No dije sino Fili —respondió don Quijote—, y éste, sin duda, es el nombre de la dama de quien se queja el autor deste soneto; y a fe que debe de ser razonable poeta, o yo sé poco del arte.
t: — I said only Fili —replied Don Quixote—, and this is, without a doubt, the name of the lady of whom the author of this sonnet complains; and by my faith, he must be a reasonable poet, or I know little of the art.

o: — Luego, ¿también —dijo Sancho— se le entiende a vuestra merced de trovas?
t: — Then, does your grace understand verses as well? —said Sancho—.

o: — Y más de lo que tú piensas —respondió don Quijote—, y veráslo cuando lleves una carta, escrita en verso de arriba abajo, a mi señora Dulcinea del Toboso.
t: "— And more than you think," replied Don Quixote, "and you will see it when you carry a letter, written in verse from top to bottom, to my lady Dulcinea of Toboso."

o: Porque quiero que sepas, Sancho, que todos o los más caballeros andantes de la edad pasada eran grandes trovadores y grandes músicos; que estas dos habilidades, o gracias, por mejor decir, son anexas a los enamorados andantes.
t: "Because I want you to know, Sancho, that all or most of the knights-errant of former times were great troubadours and great musicians; for these two skills, or gifts, better said, are proper to lovers who wander as knights."

o: Verdad es que las coplas de los pasados caballeros tienen más de espíritu que de primor.
t: "It is true that the verses of the knights of old have more spirit than polish."

o: — Lea más vuestra merced —dijo Sancho—, que ya hallará algo que nos satisfaga.
t: "— Read further, your grace," said Sancho, "for you will soon find something that satisfies us."

o: Volvió la hoja don Quijote y dijo.
t: Don Quixote turned the page and said.

o: — Esto es prosa, y parece carta.
t: "— This is prose, and it looks like a letter."

o: — ¿Carta misiva, señor? —preguntó Sancho.
t: "— A love letter, sir?" asked Sancho.

o: — En el principio no parece sino de amores —respondió don Quijote.
t: "— At the beginning it seems to be nothing but love," replied Don Quixote.

o: — Pues lea vuestra merced alto —dijo Sancho—, que gusto mucho destas cosas de amores.
t: "— Well, then, read it aloud, your grace," said Sancho, "for I greatly relish these matters of love."

o: — Que me place —dijo don Quijote.
t: "— With pleasure," said Don Quixote.

o: Y, leyéndola alto, como Sancho se lo había rogado, vio que decía desta manera.
t: And, reading it aloud, as Sancho had begged him to, he saw that it said thus.

o: Tu falsa promesa y mi cierta desventura me llevan a parte donde antes volverán a tus oídos las nuevas de mi muerte que las razones de mis quejas.
t: Your false promise and my certain misfortune lead me to a place where the news of my death will return to your ears before the reasons for my complaints.

o: Desechásteme, ¡oh ingrata!, por quien tiene más, no por quien vale más que yo; mas si la virtud fuera riqueza que se estimara, no envidiara yo dichas ajenas ni llorara desdichas propias.
t: You cast me off, oh ungrateful one, for him who has more, not for him who is worth more than I; but if virtue were wealth, it would be prized, and I would not envy what belongs to others nor weep over my own mishaps.

o: Lo que levantó tu hermosura han derribado tus obras: por ella entendí que eras ángel, y por ellas conozco que eres mujer.
t: What your beauty raised, your deeds have cast down: through it I understood that you were an angel, and through them I know that you are a woman.

o: Quédate en paz, causadora de mi guerra, y haga el cielo que los engaños de tu esposo estén siempre encubiertos, porque tú no quedes arrepentida de lo que heciste y yo no tome venganza de lo que no deseo.
t: Rest in peace, cause of my war, and may heaven keep your husband's deceptions always hidden, so that you do not repent of what you have done and I do not take vengeance for what I do not wish.

o: Acabando de leer la carta, dijo don Quijote.
t: Having finished reading the letter, Don Quixote said.

o: — Menos por ésta que por los versos se puede sacar más de que quien la escribió es algún desdeñado amante.
t: "— From this one, less than from the verses, one can infer that whoever wrote it is some scorned lover."

o: Y, hojeando casi todo el librillo, halló otros versos y cartas, que algunos pudo leer y otros no; pero lo que todos contenían eran quejas, lamentos, desconfianzas, sabores y sinsabores, favores y desdenes, solenizados los unos y llorados los otros.
t: And, leafing through nearly the whole little book, he found other verses and letters, some of which he could read and others not; but all of them contained complaints, laments, distrusts, delights and disappointments, favors and slights, some seasoned with wit and others with tears.

o: Con gran deseo quedó el Caballero de la Triste Figura de saber quién fuese el dueño de la maleta, conjeturando, por el soneto y carta, por el dinero en oro y por las tan buenas camisas, que debía de ser de algún principal enamorado, a quien desdenes y malos tratamientos de su dama debían de haber conducido a algún desesperado término.
t: The Knight of the Sorrowful Figure remained greatly desirous of knowing who the owner of the valise might be, conjecturing, from the sonnet and the letter, from the money in gold and from the very fine shirts, that it must belong to some noble lover, whom his lady's slights and ill treatment must have driven to some desperate end.

o: Pero, como por aquel lugar inhabitable y escabroso no parecía persona alguna de quien poder informarse, no se curó de más que de pasar adelante, sin llevar otro camino que aquel que Rocinante quería, que era por donde él podía caminar, siempre con imaginación que no podía faltar por aquellas malezas alguna estraña aventura.
t: But since in that uninhabitable and rugged place no person seemed to be about whom he might inquire, he did no more than press on, taking no road other than the one Rocinante chose, which was wherever he could walk, always with an imagination that could not fail to find some strange adventure among those thickets.

o: Yendo, pues, con este pensamiento, vio que, por cima de una montañuela que delante de los ojos se le ofrecía, iba saltando un hombre, de risco en risco y de mata en mata, con estraña ligereza.
t: So, going along with this thought, he saw that on top of a small hill that rose before his eyes a man was hopping along, from crag to crag and from bush to bush, with strange lightness.

o: Figurósele que iba desnudo, la barba negra y espesa, los cabellos muchos y rabultados, los pies descalzos y las piernas sin cosa alguna; los muslos cubrían unos calzones, al parecer de terciopelo leonado, mas tan hechos pedazos que por muchas partes se le descubrían las carnes.
t: He pictured him to himself as naked, with a black and bushy beard, long and tangled hair, bare feet and legs with nothing on them; his thighs were covered by breeches that seemed to be tawny velvet, but so torn to pieces that in many places his flesh was showing through.

o: Traía la cabeza descubierta, y, aunque pasó con la ligereza que se ha dicho, todas estas menudencias miró y notó el Caballero de la Triste Figura; y, aunque lo procuró, no pudo seguille, porque no era dado a la debilidad de Rocinante andar por aquellas asperezas, y más siendo él de suyo pisacorto y flemático.
t: He carried his head bare, and although he passed with the lightness already described, the Knight of the Sorrowful Countenance observed and noted all these trifling details; and though he tried, he could not follow him, for Rocinante was not given to such rough going, and he himself was short-legged and phlegmatic by nature.

o: — No podré hacer eso —respondió Sancho—, porque, en apartándome de vuestra merced, luego es conmigo el miedo, que me asalta con mil géneros de sobresaltos y visiones.
t: "I cannot do that," answered Sancho, "for once I am parted from your grace, fear comes at once upon me, assailing me with a thousand kinds of terrors and visions."

o: Y sírvale esto que digo de aviso, para que de aquí adelante no me aparte un dedo de su presencia.
t: And let this serve as the warning I give you, so that from now on you never stray a finger's breadth from my presence.

o: — Así será —dijo el de la Triste Figura—, y yo estoy muy contento de que te quieras valer de mi ánimo, el cual no te ha de faltar, aunque te falte el ánima del cuerpo.
t: "So it shall be," said the Knight of the Sorrowful Countenance, "and I am very glad that you wish to rely on my courage, which shall never fail you, though your own body should fail you."

o: Y vente ahora tras mí poco a poco, o como pudieres, y haz de los ojos lanternas; rodearemos esta serrezuela: quizá toparemos con aquel hombre que vimos, el cual, sin duda alguna, no es otro que el dueño de nuestro hallazgo.
t: Now come along behind me as slowly as you can, or as best you are able, and make eyes of your head like lanterns; we will go around this little hill: perhaps we shall come upon that man we saw, who is without a doubt none other than the owner of our find.

o: A lo que Sancho respondió.
t: To which Sancho made no answer.

o: — Engáñaste en eso, Sancho —respondió don Quijote—; que, ya que hemos caído en sospecha de quién es el dueño, cuasi delante, estamos obligados a buscarle y volvérselos; y, cuando no le buscásemos, la vehemente sospecha que tenemos de que él lo sea nos pone ya en tanta culpa como si lo fuese.
t: "You are mistaken in that, Sancho," replied Don Quixote; "for since we have fallen under suspicion of who the owner is, and he is almost before us, we are bound to seek him out and return what is his; and even if we did not seek him, the strong suspicion we have that he is the owner already holds us as guilty as if he were."

o: Así que, Sancho amigo, no te dé pena el buscalle, por la que a mí se me quitará si le hallo.
t: So, friend Sancho, do not let it trouble you to look for him, for I shall be rid of that trouble if I find him.

o: Y así, picó a Rocinante, y siguióle Sancho con su acostumbrado jumento; y, habiendo rodeado parte de la montaña, hallaron en un arroyo, caída, muerta y medio comida de perros y picada de grajos, una mula ensillada y enfrenada; todo lo cual confirmó en ellos más la sospecha de que aquel que huía era el dueño de la mula y del cojín.
t: And so he spurred Rocinante on, and Sancho followed him on his accustomed donkey; and having gone around part of the mountain, they found in a brook a mule, saddled and bridled, fallen, dead, and half eaten by dogs and picked at by crows; all of which confirmed them the more in the suspicion that the one who had fled was the owner of the mule and the saddlebag.

o: Estándola mirando, oyeron un silbo como de pastor que guardaba ganado, y a deshora, a su siniestra mano, parecieron una buena cantidad de cabras, y tras ellas, por cima de la montaña, pareció el cabrero que las guardaba, que era un hombre anciano.
t: While they were looking at it, they heard a whistle like that of a shepherd minding his flock, and at an untimely hour, at his sinister hand, there appeared a good number of goats, and behind them, over the top of the mountain, there appeared the goatherd who had them in charge, who was an old man.

o: Diole voces don Quijote, y rogóle que bajase donde estaban.
t: Don Quixote called out to him and begged him to come down to where they were.

o: Él respondió a gritos que quién les había traído por aquel lugar, pocas o ningunas veces pisado sino de pies de cabras o de lobos y otras fieras que por allí andaban.
t: He shouted back in reply that who had ever brought them to that place, trodden few or no times save by the feet of goats or wolves and other wild beasts that roamed about there.

o: Respondióle Sancho que bajase, que de todo le darían buena cuenta.
t: Sancho told him to come down, and they would give him a full account of everything.

o: Bajó el cabrero, y, en llegando adonde don Quijote estaba, dijo.
t: The goatherd came down, and when he reached where Don Quixote was, he said:

o: — Apostaré que está mirando la mula de alquiler que está muerta en esa hondonada.
t: "I will wager that he is looking at the hired mule that lies dead in that hollow."

o: Pues a buena fe que ha ya seis meses que está en ese lugar.
t: "As for that, it has been in that spot for six months now."

o: Díganme: ¿han topado por ahí a su dueño?
t: "Tell me: have you happened upon her owner anywhere around here?"

o: — No hemos topado a nadie —respondió don Quijote—, sino a un cojín y a una maletilla que no lejos deste lugar hallamos.
t: "We have met no one," answered Don Quixote, "except a saddlebag and a valise, which we found not far from this place."

o: — También la hallé yo —respondió el cabrero—, mas nunca la quise alzar ni llegar a ella, temeroso de algún desmán y de que no me la pidiesen por de hurto; que es el diablo sotil, y debajo de los pies se levanta allombre cosa donde tropiece y caya, sin saber cómo ni cómo no.
t: — I found it too," answered the goatherd, "but I never cared to pick it up or come near it, fearing some mishap and that they might claim it from me as stolen; for the devil is subtle, and underfoot he raises some snare where you stumble and fall, without knowing how or how not.

o: — Eso mesmo es lo que yo digo —respondió Sancho—: que también la hallé yo, y no quise llegar a ella con un tiro de piedra; allí la dejé y allí se queda como se estaba, que no quiero perro con cencerro.
t: — That is exactly what I say," answered Sancho, "for I found it too, and I did not care to come near it within a stone's throw; there I left it, and there it stays as it was, for I don't want a dog with a bell around its neck."

o: — Decidme, buen hombre —dijo don Quijote—, ¿sabéis vos quién sea el dueño destas prendas?
t: — Tell me, good man," said Don Quixote, "do you know who the owner of these garments is?"

o: — Lo que sabré yo decir —dijo el cabrero— es que «habrá al pie de seis meses, poco más a menos, que llegó a una majada de pastores, que estará como tres leguas deste lugar, un mancebo de gentil talle y apostura, caballero sobre esa mesma mula que ahí está muerta, y con el mesmo cojín y maleta que decís que hallastes y no tocastes.
t: — What I can tell you," said the goatherd, "is that 'within the foot of six months, more or less, there arrived at a shepherd's fold about three leagues from this place a youth of fine bearing and comeliness, mounted on that very mule which lies dead there, with the same cushion and valise that you say you found and did not touch.'"

o: Preguntónos que cuál parte desta sierra era la más áspera y escondida; dijímosle que era esta donde ahora estamos; y es ansí la verdad, porque si entráis media legua más adentro, quizá no acertaréis a salir; y estoy maravillado de cómo habéis podido llegar aquí, porque no hay camino ni senda que a este lugar encamine.
t: He asked us which part of this sierra was the roughest and most hidden; we told him it was the one where we are now; and that is the truth, for if you go half a league further in, you will perhaps fail to find your way out; and I marvel how you could have got here, for there is no road or path leading to this place.

o: Como esto supimos algunos cabreros, le anduvimos a buscar casi dos días por lo más cerrado desta sierra, al cabo de los cuales le hallamos metido en el hueco de un grueso y valiente alcornoque.
t: When we goatherds learned this, we went looking for him for nearly two days through the thickest of this sierra, and at the end of them we found him sheltering in the hollow of a thick and sturdy holm oak.

o: Salió a nosotros con mucha mansedumbre, ya roto el vestido, y el rostro disfigurado y tostado del sol, de tal suerte que apenas le conocíamos, sino que los vestidos, aunque rotos, con la noticia que dellos teníamos, nos dieron a entender que era el que buscábamos.
t: He came out to us very meekly, his clothes already torn, his face disfigured and scorched by the sun, so that we barely knew him; only the clothes, though torn, together with what we had heard about them, made us understand that he was the one we were looking for.

o: Saludónos cortésmente, y en pocas y muy buenas razones nos dijo que no nos maravillásemos de verle andar de aquella suerte, porque así le convenía para cumplir cierta penitencia que por sus muchos pecados le había sido impuesta.
t: He greeted us courteously, and in a few well-chosen words told us not to be amazed at seeing him in that condition, for it was fitting for him to perform a certain penance which had been imposed on him for his many sins.

o: Rogámosle que nos dijese quién era, mas nunca lo pudimos acabar con él.
t: We asked him to tell us who he was, but we could never get it out of him.

o: Pedímosle también que, cuando hubiese menester el sustento, sin el cual no podía pasar, nos dijese dónde le hallaríamos, porque con mucho amor y cuidado se lo llevaríamos; y que si esto tampoco fuese de su gusto, que, a lo menos, saliese a pedirlo, y no a quitarlo a los pastores.
t: We also asked him that, whenever he should need sustenance, without which he could not live, he would tell us where we might find him, because we would gladly and carefully take it to him; and that if this too were not to his liking, he should at least come out and ask for it, and not take it from the shepherds by force.

o: Agradeció nuestro ofrecimiento, pidió perdón de los asaltos pasados, y ofreció de pedillo de allí adelante por amor de Dios, sin dar molestia alguna a nadie.
t: He thanked our offer, asked pardon for the past outrages, and promised to ask for it henceforth for the love of God, without causing anyone any trouble.

o: En cuanto lo que tocaba a la estancia de su habitación, dijo que no tenía otra que aquella que le ofrecía la ocasión donde le tomaba la noche; y acabó su plática con un tan tierno llanto, que bien fuéramos de piedra los que escuchado le habíamos, si en él no le acompañáramos, considerándole cómo le habíamos visto la vez primera, y cuál le veíamos entonces.
t: As for where he was to stay, he said he had no other place than the one the occasion offered him, where the night overtook him; and he ended his talk with such tender weeping that we who had listened to him would have been made of stone if we had not wept with him, considering how we had seen him the first time and how we saw him then.

o: Porque, como tengo dicho, era un muy gentil y agraciado mancebo, y en sus corteses y concertadas razones mostraba ser bien nacido y muy cortesana persona; que, puesto que éramos rústicos los que le escuchábamos, su gentileza era tanta, que bastaba a darse a conocer a la mesma rusticidad.
t: For, as I have said, he was a very gallant and graceful youth, and in his courteous and measured words he showed himself well-born and a very courtly man; and though we who listened to him were rustic folk, his gentility was such that it sufficed for even rusticity to recognize itself in him.

o: Mas él nos dio a entender presto ser verdad lo que pensábamos, porque se levantó con gran furia del suelo, donde se había echado, y arremetió con el primero que halló junto a sí, con tal denuedo y rabia que, si no se le quitáramos, le matara a puñadas y a bocados; y todo esto hacía, diciendo: ''¡Ah, fementido Fernando!
t: But he soon made us understand that what we thought was true, for he rose with great fury from the ground, where he had thrown himself, and rushed at the first man he found beside him, with such boldness and rage that, had we not pulled him away, he would have killed him with his fists and his teeth; and all this he did, crying: 'Ah, lying Fernando!'"

o: ¡Aquí, aquí me pagarás la sinrazón que me heciste: estas manos te sacarán el corazón, donde albergan y tienen manida todas las maldades juntas, principalmente la fraude y el engaño!'' Y a éstas añadía otras razones, que todas se encaminaban a decir mal de aquel Fernando y a tacharle de traidor y fementido.
t: 'Here, here you shall pay me for the wrong you did me: these hands will tear out your heart, where all the wickednesses dwell together, above all fraud and deceit!' And to these he added other sayings, all tending to speak ill of that Fernando and to brand him a traitor and a liar.

o: Quitámossele, pues, con no poca pesadumbre, y él, sin decir más palabra, se apartó de nosotros y se emboscó corriendo por entre estos jarales y malezas, de modo que nos imposibilitó el seguille.
t: We took him away from them, therefore, with no little effort, and he, without saying another word, withdrew from us and hid himself running among these thickets and brushwood, so that he made it impossible for us to follow him.

o: Por esto conjeturamos que la locura le venía a tiempos, y que alguno que se llamaba Fernando le debía de haber hecho alguna mala obra, tan pesada cuanto lo mostraba el término a que le había conducido.
t: From this we conjectured that his madness came upon him at times, and that someone named Fernando must have done him some ill, so heavy as the end to which it had brought him showed.

o: Esto es, señores, lo que sabré deciros de lo que me habéis preguntado; y entended que el dueño de las prendas que hallastes es el mesmo que vistes pasar con tanta ligereza como desnudez —que ya le había dicho don Quijote cómo había visto pasar aquel hombre saltando por la sierra.
t: This, gentlemen, is what I can tell you of what you have asked me; and understand that the owner of the garments you found is the same man you saw pass by with such lightness as nakedness—for Don Quixote had already told him how he had seen that man leaping across the sierra.

o: El cual quedó admirado de lo que al cabrero había oído, y quedó con más deseo de saber quién era el desdichado loco; y propuso en sí lo mesmo que ya tenía pensado: de buscalle por toda la montaña, sin dejar rincón ni cueva en ella que no mirase, hasta hallarle.
t: He was astonished at what he had heard from the goatherd, and he became more eager to know who the unhappy madman was; and he resolved within himself the same thing he had already planned: to search for him throughout the mountain, leaving no corner or cave in it unexamined, until he found him.

o: Pero hízolo mejor la suerte de lo que él pensaba ni esperaba, porque en aquel mesmo instante pareció, por entre una quebrada de una sierra que salía donde ellos estaban, el mancebo que buscaba, el cual venía hablando entre sí cosas que no podían ser entendidas de cerca, cuanto más de lejos.
t: But fortune did it better than he thought or hoped, for at that very instant the youth he was seeking appeared through a ravine of a sierra that came out where they were, and he was talking to himself about things that could not be heard close by, let alone from afar.

o: Su traje era cual se ha pintado, sólo que, llegando cerca, vio don Quijote que un coleto hecho pedazos que sobre sí traía era de ámbar; por donde acabó de entender que persona que tales hábitos traía no debía de ser de ínfima calidad.
t: His suit was as if it had been painted, but, coming closer, Don Quixote saw that the jerkin he wore, all in tatters, was of amber; whereby he came to understand that a person who wore such garments could not be of the lowest station.

o: En llegando el mancebo a ellos, les saludó con una voz desentonada y bronca, pero con mucha cortesía.
t: When the youth reached them, he greeted them with a discordant, hoarse voice, but with great courtesy.

o: Don Quijote le volvió las saludes con no menos comedimiento, y, apeándose de Rocinante, con gentil continente y donaire, le fue a abrazar y le tuvo un buen espacio estrechamente entre sus brazos, como si de luengos tiempos le hubiera conocido.
t: Don Quixote returned his greetings with no less courtesy, and, dismounting from Rocinante, with gentle bearing and grace, went to embrace him and held him tightly in his arms for a good while, as though he had known him for many long years.

o: En resolución, el primero que habló después del abrazamiento fue el Roto, y dijo lo que se dirá adelante.
t: In short, the first to speak after the embrace was the Roto, who said what will be told hereafter.
